337:     process.env.PAYMENT_ENCRYPTION_KEY ||

346: /** Mismo formato que server/security.ts (AES-256-GCM, base64url). */
347: function encryptSensitive(plaintext) {
348:   const value = String(plaintext ?? "").trim();
349:   if (!value) return null;
350:   const iv = crypto.randomBytes(12);
351:   const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", paymentKey(), iv);
352:   const encrypted = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(value, "utf8"), cipher.final()]);
353:   const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();
354:   return `enc:v1:${iv.toString("base64url")}:${tag.toString("base64url")}:${encrypted.toString("base64url")}`;

## Objective
- Añadir una sección de perfil donde el usuario pueda personalizar nombre, avatar, banner y datos de contacto.
- Integrar prácticas de seguridad y actualizar el schema de la base de datos (permiso explícito del usuario).

## Requirements
- Personalización de: nombre, imagen de avatar, banner y contacto.
- Incluir validaciones y prácticas de seguridad tras implementar la funcionalidad.
- Se permite modificar `shared/schema.ts` y la base de datos.
- UI en español, coherente con el estilo existente (React + Tailwind + componentes shadcn).

## Decisions
- Añadir columnas `banner_url`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `contact_website`, `contact_visibility` a `users`.
- `contact_visibility` con valores `public | followers | private`, por defecto `private` (minimización de datos).
- Validación de imágenes de perfil: solo HTTPS, hosts aprobados (`res.cloudinary.com`, `*.googleusercontent.com`, etc.), sin credenciales/puertos/IPs privadas.
- Sitio web de contacto: solo HTTPS público, sin credenciales ni hosts privados.
- Email de contacto con regex estricta; teléfono validado por formato y cantidad de dígitos.
- El perfil público solo expone contacto según visibilidad, seguimiento y estado de bloqueo.
- Nueva página `/profile` para edición; `/u/:username` se mantiene como perfil público.
- Migración idempotente vía `ensureUserSchema` y `scripts/security-migration.mjs`.

### Completed
- Schema actualizado en `shared/schema.ts`.
- `server/security.ts`: nuevos campos en `PublicUser`/`sanitizeUser`; validadores `validateProfileImageUrl`, `validateAvatarUrl`, `validateBannerUrl`, `validateContactWebsite`, `isValidContactEmail`, `isValidContactPhone`, `isValidContactVisibility`, `normalizeContactVisibility`, `isPrivateHostname`, `sanitizeProfileText`, `sanitizeProfileBio`.

Use that path literally rather than guessing at a home directory. | option | meaning | |---|---| | `--snapshot` | list every interactive element with a clickable ref (add `--full` for the whole accessibility tree) | | `--wait ` | block until the selector appears (default: DOM ready) | | `--eval ` | run an expression in the page, print the JSON result | | `--script ` | drive a sequence — see **Scripting** below | | `--screenshot

` | write a PNG — read it afterwards to look at it | | `--timeout ` | navigation timeout, default 30000 | | `--session ` | keep ONE page alive across calls — see **Sessions** below | | `--close` | with `--session `, tear that session's browser down | ## Driving by ref, not by selector `--snapshot` returns the page's interactive elements, each with a ref: ``` @e5 button "Audit my code" @e9 button "Select your model" [haspopup=menu] @e10 button "Manual" [haspopup=menu] @e11 button "Send" [disabled] ``` Click `@e10` and you get what the page says is there — no selector to author from a DOM you cannot see. A ref is stamped into the page, so it dies on navigation or a re-render. **Re-snapshot after anything that changes the page** — the refs renumber, and a stale one matches nothing. `--full` returns the accessibility tree instead (headings, text, links). Use refs to *act*, `--full` to *read*. ## Scripting a sequence `--script` runs a file that default-exports `async (page, ui) => result`. **`page` is a Playwright `Page`** (the driver is patchright, a Playwright fork), so use the Playwright API — `page.locator`, `page.getByRole`, `page.getByText`, `page.waitForFunction`, `page.evaluate`. The runner owns the browser, the console/network capture and the teardown; the script only drives and asserts. ```js // qa.mjs — node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --script ./qa.mjs export default async function run(page, ui) { // Look at what is there before deciding what to click. const before = await ui.snapshot() const signIn = before.match(/@(e\d+) button "Sign in"/)?.[1] if (!signIn) return { error: 'no sign-in button', snapshot: before } await ui.click(signIn) await page.waitForTimeout(500) // The page changed, so the old refs are gone — snapshot again. const after = await ui.snapshot() return { opened: after.includes('textbox'), after } } ``` Navigation to the URL argument has already happened before your function runs. You can navigate further with `page.goto(...)`. ## Text for structure, a screenshot for anything visual Use the text reports for structure, content and state: - `--snapshot` — every interactive element, with refs - `--snapshot --full` — the accessibility tree: headings, text, links - `--eval "…"` — ask the DOM a direct question - the console/network report, which catches most breakage for almost nothing For anything visual — a page you built or restyled, a layout, a chart, a game screen — take a screenshot and read it before you say the work is done. `--screenshot` writes a PNG and **you can read it**: a read of an image returns the picture. Check it for overlapping or clipped text, broken images and blank regions, and for whether it matches what was asked, and say what you saw. If the read comes back as `[binary file: png …]`, you cannot see images here: say so, and verify with `--snapshot --full` and `--eval` instead of guessing at what rendered. One screenshot per visual change is enough; you do not need one per step. ## Interpreting the report - `console.error` / uncaught exceptions → almost always a real bug. - `requests failed` → a 404 on a JS chunk usually means a stale build is being served; a 500 means the server, not the page. - `title` empty and `bodyChars` near zero → the app did not mount at all.
